title: Projects
subtitle: A collection of self-hosted applications and tools I have built and maintain.

homelab.name: Homelab
homelab.shortDescription: Self-hosted infrastructure running on a home server, orchestrated with Kubernetes (k3s) and managed with Docker, Traefik, and automated deployment pipelines.
homelab.description: A personal homelab environment built for learning and running self-hosted services. The infrastructure runs on a dedicated server using Kubernetes (k3s) for container orchestration, Traefik as a reverse proxy and ingress controller, and PostgreSQL databases for persistent storage. All projects are containerised with Docker and deployed via automated scripts and Makefiles. The setup includes SSL certificate management, monitoring, and CI/CD workflows.

features.f2: Traefik reverse proxy with automatic SSL via Let's Encrypt
features.f3: PostgreSQL databases with persistent volume claims

cards.name: Cards
cards.shortDescription: A self-hosted card-game scoring and leaderboard platform for tracking results across multiple Belgian and Dutch card games, with ELO ratings and player profiles.
cards.description: A full-stack scoring platform designed for tracking card game results among friends. Supports Whist, Color Whist, King, Double King, Manille, Press, and Hearts. Each player has a profile with per-game-type ELO ratings, win rates, average scores, and game history. Features a global leaderboard, ELO comparison charts, an admin panel for managing players and recalculating ratings, and optional email notifications for game results.

features.f1: Multi-game support: Whist, Color Whist, King, Double King, Manille, Press, Hearts
features.f2: Per-game-type ELO rating system with full history and comparison charts
features.f3: Global and per-game leaderboards with win rate, average score, and records
features.f4: Player profiles with game history and ELO graphs
features.f5: Optional SMTP email notifications for game results and daily digests
features.f6: Admin panel for player management, ELO recalculation, and configuration

cardsApp.name: Cards App
cardsApp.shortDescription: A native Android and desktop app that embeds the Cards platform in a fullscreen Tauri WebView with a local rewriting proxy for seamless framing.
cardsApp.description: A cross-platform app built with Tauri 2 and Vue 3 that wraps the Cards web application in a native fullscreen WebView. It includes a local HTTP proxy that strips frame-busting headers, rewrites resource URLs, and injects navigation tracking so the embedded site renders and behaves correctly inside the app. Supports Android and desktop platforms with zero extra UI overhead.

features.f1: Fullscreen embedded view of the Cards web application
features.f2: Local rewriting proxy that strips X-Frame-Options and CSP headers
features.f3: Automatic URL rewriting for resources and CSS
features.f4: Safe-area padding for Android notch and status bar
features.f5: Cross-platform: Android (APK) and desktop (Linux, macOS, Windows)

notes.name: Notes
notes.shortDescription: A self-hosted productivity suite with a rich-text note editor, Trello-style kanban boards, a calendar, and visual graph diagrams with Google SSO.
notes.description: A full-featured self-hosted productivity application combining multiple tools in a single platform. The rich-text editor is powered by Tiptap and supports headings, lists, tables, code blocks, links, images, and file attachments. The kanban board module offers multiple boards with drag-and-drop cards, labels, due dates, and checklists. Includes a calendar with recurring events and a graph module for visual node-and-edge diagrams that can reference notes, boards, or cards. All data is isolated per user with JWT authentication and optional Google OAuth SSO.

features.f1: Rich-text editor with Tiptap: headings, lists, tables, code blocks, images, attachments
features.f2: Folder organisation with nested folders and full-text search
features.f4: Kanban boards with drag-and-drop cards, labels, due dates, and checklists
features.f5: Calendar with recurring events and automation triggers
features.f6: Visual graph diagrams with nodes referencing notes, boards, or cards
features.f7: Google OAuth SSO and per-user data isolation

stack.frontend: Vue 3 / TypeScript / Vite / Tiptap / Pinia / VueDraggable

notesApp.name: Notes App
notesApp.shortDescription: A native Android and desktop app for the Notes backend, featuring a rich-text editor, folder tree navigation, and Google OAuth sign-in.
notesApp.description: A cross-platform mobile and desktop client for the Notes server built with Tauri 2 and Vue 3. Features the full Tiptap rich-text editor with bold, italic, headings, lists, tables, code blocks, and images. Includes a collapsible folder tree sidebar with drag-and-drop, note search and filtering, attachment viewing, and a settings screen for configuring the API URL. Authentication uses native Android Google Sign-In via a JNI bridge, with a browser redirect fallback on desktop.

features.f1: Rich-text editor powered by Tiptap with full formatting support
features.f2: Folder tree with nested folders and drag-and-drop
features.f3: Note search, sort, and filter by folder
features.f5: Google OAuth SSO via native Android JNI bridge

music.name: Music
music.shortDescription: A self-hosted music library, streaming server, and DJ toolset with YouTube downloading, BPM/key detection, and Rekordbox export.
music.description: A comprehensive self-hosted music management platform built for personal use. Upload and organise audio files with automatic metadata extraction, duplicate detection, and file sync from a mounted directory. Stream tracks directly in the browser via a WaveSurfer.js waveform player. Download from YouTube with real-time progress via Server-Sent Events, manage playlists with Rekordbox XML export, and maintain a clean genre and artist taxonomy with Discogs-based metadata enrichment. Includes BPM detection via aubio, key detection, and an admin panel with audit logging.

features.f1: Audio upload with automatic metadata extraction and duplicate detection
features.f2: In-browser waveform player powered by WaveSurfer.js
features.f3: YouTube downloading (single and playlist) with real-time progress
features.f4: Playlist management with ZIP and Rekordbox XML export
features.f5: BPM and key detection using aubio and FFT analysis
features.f6: Genre taxonomy with aliases, Discogs enrichment, and metadata suggestion queue
features.f7: Admin panel with audit log, bulk rename, and auto-download scheduler

musicApp.name: Music App
musicApp.shortDescription: A native Android and desktop app for the Music server with library browsing, streaming, playlist management, and a two-deck DJ mixing interface.
musicApp.description: A cross-platform mobile and desktop client for the MusicServer backend built with Tauri 2 and Vue 3. Browse the full music library with search, artist, and genre filters. Stream tracks with a persistent bottom player bar featuring play, pause, seek, shuffle, and queue management. Includes an artist browser, playlist viewer, and a two-deck DJ mixing interface where tracks can be loaded from the library onto individual decks with independent playback controls. Authentication via native Android Google Sign-In with a configurable API URL.

features.f1: Library browsing with search, artist, and genre filters
features.f2: Persistent player bar with play, pause, seek, shuffle, and queue
features.f3: Full track streaming from the Music server backend
features.f5: Two-deck DJ mixing interface with independent controls
features.f6: Google OAuth SSO via native Android JNI bridge

kholisa32.name: Kholisa-32
kholisa32.shortDescription: A custom handheld game console built around an STM32F746NG microcontroller, running a custom bytecode virtual machine and rendering games on a 4.3" 480x272 LCD with touch input.
kholisa32.description: Kholisa-32 is a custom handheld game console built on the STM32F746G-DISCO discovery board (Cortex-M7, 216 MHz). Games are written in a custom assembly language, compiled to bytecode on a PC, and transferred to the device over UART. The virtual machine executes 32-bit wide instructions with 256 general-purpose registers, a call stack, and a full instruction set covering arithmetic, bitwise logic, conditional branching, and display drawing. Games are stored in 16 MB QSPI NOR flash and rendered via DMA2D onto an SDRAM framebuffer displayed on the RK043FN48H 4.3" capacitive touch LCD.

features.f1: Custom bytecode virtual machine with 256 registers and a 32-bit instruction set
features.f2: 4.3" 480x272 TFT LCD with capacitive touch input (FT5336)
features.f3: 16 MB QSPI NOR flash for game storage; up to 10 games in a touch-based launcher
features.f4: DMA2D-accelerated rendering to an SDRAM framebuffer
features.f5: UART game upload protocol with packet-based transfer and ACK handshake
features.f6: Drawing primitives: lines, rectangles, circles, images, and text
features.f7: Built with STM32CubeIDE using STM32 HAL and BSP drivers

kholisa32Ide.name: Kholisa-32 IDE
kholisa32Ide.shortDescription: A desktop IDE for writing, compiling, linking, and uploading games to the Kholisa-32 console, built with Python and PySide2.
kholisa32Ide.description: A Python desktop application built with PySide2 (Qt for Python) for developing games for the Kholisa-32 console. The IDE provides a source editor for the custom .khl assembly language, a compiler that produces intermediate hex output in two passes, a linker that assembles the final .khr binary with header, icon, sprite, and sound sections, and a UART transfer module that uploads binaries to the device over serial. Asset helpers let you attach PNG icons and sprites (auto-converted to ARGB1555) and WAV sound files directly from the Build menu. Port and baud rate are configurable from the Options menu and persisted in a settings file.

features.f1: Source editor for the .khl custom assembly language with unsaved-changes indicator
features.f2: Two-pass compiler: instruction encoding and label resolution
features.f3: Linker that produces .khr binaries with header, icon, sprites, and sounds
features.f4: UART upload with packet-based transfer and ACK handshake
features.f6: Configurable serial port and baud rate, persisted in settings.conf
